title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat, report what is broken, get the landlord to have it fixed, sort out bills and the building, and deal politely with neighbours and noise.
intro:
If you live in India for more than a few weeks, sooner or later the geyser stops working, the tap drips, the lift is 'under maintenance' and the people upstairs are having a party at midnight. This unit gives you the Hindi to handle all of it: renting words (most of them English!), describing what's wrong, asking the landlord to *get it fixed*, and complaining to a neighbour without starting a feud.

The two skills are **complaining politely but firmly** and the **causative** (करवाना, बदलवाना, लगवाना), which you met in the errands unit. Here you'll use it the way tenants really do: मकान-मालिक जी, आप ठीक करवा दीजिए!

grammar.title: Complaining politely but firmly
grammar.body:
A good complaint in Hindi has two halves: **say what's wrong**, then **ask for what you want**. Keep the polite forms (आप, जी, -इए) even when you are annoyed — in Hindi, firmness comes from facts and repetition, not from dropping to तुम.

**1. Saying what's wrong**
X **ख़राब है** / **ख़राब हो गया है** — X is broken / has broken down
X **काम नहीं कर रहा** — X isn't working
X **टपक रहा है** · बिजली **नहीं आ रही** — X is dripping · there's no power
मुझे X **से परेशानी हो रही है** — X is bothering me

In speech the final **है** of the continuous is usually dropped after नहीं (काम नहीं कर रहा), but **रहा / रही / रहे** stays, and it agrees with the thing: नल टपक **रहा** है, लिफ़्ट नहीं चल **रही**.

**2. Asking, from soft to firm**
**ज़रा** … **कर दीजिए** — just … please (दे adds 'for me', and sounds smoother)
**क्या आप … देंगे?** — would you …?
… **कर दीजिएगा** — please do … (extra polite, slightly 'when you can')
**आज ही** … — … today itself (**ही** = 'this very')

**3. Pushing a little** — add facts: **कब से** (दो हफ़्ते **से** 'for two weeks'), **बार-बार** 'again and again', **फिर भी** 'and still', **मैंने कितनी बार कहा है** 'how many times have I said'. Neighbours get the softest version: a **थोड़ा** and a smile go a long way.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: having the landlord get it done
grammar.body:
You know the causative from the errands unit: add **-वा-** to the stem when someone **else** does the job. Around the house you'll use these all the time:

ठीक करना → **ठीक करवाना** 'get fixed' · लगाना → **लगवाना** 'get installed' · बदलना → **बदलवाना** 'get replaced' · बनाना → **बनवाना** 'get made' · साफ़ करना → **साफ़ करवाना** 'get cleaned'

**Who does the work** takes **से**: मैंने **प्लंबर से** नल ठीक करवाया 'I had the plumber fix the tap'.

**Who arranges it** is the subject. That is the whole point when you rent: मकान-मालिक ठीक **करवाएगा** 'the landlord will get it fixed' — not you, and not with your money!

**Asking someone to arrange it**: causative + **दीजिए** — आप ठीक **करवा दीजिए** 'please get it fixed'. **Arranging it for yourself**: causative + **लेना** — मैं ख़ुद **करवा लूँगी** 'I'll get it done myself'.

**I need to get … done**: मुझे … करवाना **है** / करवाना **पड़ेगा** 'I'll have to'. The infinitive agrees with a feminine thing: मुझे नई बत्ती **लगवानी** है.

The trap: ठीक **कर** दीजिए asks the person to fix it with their own hands; ठीक **करवा** दीजिए asks them to get someone to fix it. Say the second to a landlord.

examples.en: I need to get the geyser fixed.
I had the plumber replace the tap.

culture:
In Indian cities the landlord often lives in the same building — upstairs, or on the ground floor — so renting is a personal relationship. Tenants call the landlord **uncle/aunty** or **Gupta ji**, always with **आप**, and complaints are made by phone or on WhatsApp with plenty of **जी** and **प्लीज़**. Expect to pay a **broker** (ब्रोकर, often a month's rent), an **advance/deposit**, and to sign an **11-month agreement**. Some landlords still prefer families to 'bachelors' or ask about your diet — frustrating, but common; it's worth asking up front.

Neighbours matter. Older neighbours will call you **बेटा/बेटी** and use **तुम**, ask personal questions, and may complain indirectly ('Mr Sharma upstairs was saying…') rather than to your face; answer warmly and say **आगे से ध्यान रखूँगा/रखूँगी** 'I'll be careful from now on'. When you move in, it's a nice touch to introduce yourself and maybe take sweets round. Daily life runs on the **guard**, the **rubbish collector**, the **water timings** and the **society WhatsApp group**, where every complaint about parking eventually ends up.

tip.title: Renting words
tip.body:
- The owner is the **मकान-मालिक** (called *uncle*, *aunty* or *Gupta ji* to their face); you are the **किरायेदार**.
- Most renting words are English — **फ़्लैट, ब्रोकर, एडवांस, एग्रीमेंट, मेंटेनेंस** — used with Hindi grammar: एडवांस **कितना** देना होगा?
- Use **आप** with landlords and brokers, whatever their age.

tip.title: … काम नहीं कर रहा — saying what's wrong
tip.body:
- **X ख़राब है / ख़राब हो गया है** — X is broken / has broken down.
- **X काम नहीं कर रहा** — X isn't working. In speech the last **है** is often dropped, but never **रहा / रही**.
- रहा/रही/रहे agrees with the thing: नल टपक **रहा** है, लिफ़्ट नहीं चल **रही**.
- Say since when with **से**: दो दिन **से** 'for two days'.

lessons.title: Getting the landlord to fix it

tip.title: ठीक करवा दीजिए — get it fixed, please
tip.body:
- Causative **-वा-** = someone else does the job: **लगवाना** get installed, **बदलवाना** get replaced, **ठीक करवाना** get fixed.
- The worker takes **से**: प्लंबर **से** नल ठीक करवाया.
- To the landlord: ठीक **करवा दीजिए** — not ठीक **कर** दीजिए, which asks him to do it himself.
- 'I need to get it done': मुझे … करवाना **है**.

sentences.native: इलेक्ट्रीशियन शाम तक आ जाएगा।
sentences.roman: ilekṭrīshiyan shām tak ā jāyegā.
sentences.en: The electrician will come by the evening.

sentences.native: मैंने तीन बार फ़ोन किया, पर कोई नहीं उठा रहा।
sentences.roman: maiṃne tīn bār fon kiyā, par koī nahīṃ uṭhā rahā.
sentences.en: I called three times, but no one's picking up.

sentences.native: यहाँ पानी कब आता है, सुबह या शाम?
sentences.roman: yahāṃ pānī kab ātā hai, subah yā shām?
sentences.en: When does the water come here, morning or evening?

sentences.native: छत वाली टंकी ख़ाली है, ज़रा मोटर चला दो।
sentences.roman: chhat vālī ṭaṅkī xālī hai, zarā moṭar chalā do.
sentences.en: The tank on the roof is empty, switch on the pump, would you.

sentences.native: सोसाइटी वाले हर महीने टंकी साफ़ करवाते हैं।
sentences.roman: sosāiṭī vāle har mahīne ṭaṅkī sāf karvāte haiṃ.
sentences.en: The society gets the tank cleaned every month.

sentences.native: कूड़ा बाहर रख दो, सुबह गार्ड ले जाएगा।
sentences.roman: kūṛā bāhar rakh do, subah gārḍ le jāyegā.
sentences.en: Put the rubbish outside, the guard will take it in the morning.

sentences.native: गार्ड भैया, मेरी पार्किंग में किसी और की गाड़ी है।
sentences.roman: gārḍ bhaiyā, merī pārkiṅg meṃ kisī aur kī gāṛī hai.
sentences.en: Guard bhaiya, someone else's car is in my parking spot.

sentences.native: भैया, गाड़ी थोड़ी आगे हटा लीजिए।
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, gāṛī thoṛī āge haṭā lījiye.
sentences.en: Bhaiya, please move your car forward a little.

sentences.native: मैंने दरवाज़े का ताला बदलवा दिया।
sentences.roman: maiṃne darvāze kā tālā badalvā diyā.
sentences.en: I got the lock on the door changed.

sentences.native: सोसाइटी का मेंटेनेंस कितना है?
sentences.roman: sosāiṭī kā meṇṭenens kitnā hai?
sentences.en: How much is the society maintenance?

sentences.native: बिजली का बिल इस बार बहुत ज़्यादा आया।
sentences.roman: bijlī kā bil is bār bahut zyādā āyā.
sentences.en: The electricity bill came to a lot this time.

lessons.title: Dealing with neighbours

tip.title: Polite but firm
tip.body:
- Start soft: **ज़रा** … **कर दीजिए** · **क्या आप … देंगे?**
- Add facts: दो हफ़्ते **से** 'for two weeks', **बार-बार** 'again and again', **फिर भी** 'and still'.
- With neighbours, a **थोड़ा / थोड़ी** goes a long way: आवाज़ **थोड़ी** कम कर दीजिए.
- Getting firmer never means dropping from **आप** to तुम.

new: बार-बार कहने पर भी कोई नहीं आया।

sentences.native: ज़रा टीवी की आवाज़ कम कर दीजिए, बच्चे सो रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: zarā ṭīvī kī āvāz kam kar dījiye, bachche so rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: Could you turn the TV down a bit, the children are asleep.

sentences.native: ऊपर वाले पड़ोसी दो हफ़्ते से रोज़ रात को शोर कर रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: ūpar vāle paṛosī do hafte se roz rāt ko shor kar rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: The neighbours upstairs have been making noise every night for two weeks.

sentences.native: मैंने उनसे दो बार कहा, फिर भी शोर बंद नहीं हुआ।
sentences.roman: maiṃne unse do bār kahā, phir bhī shor band nahīṃ huā.
sentences.en: I told them twice, and still the noise didn't stop.

sentences.native: क्या आप रात दस बजे के बाद आवाज़ थोड़ी कम रखेंगे?
sentences.roman: kyā āp rāt das baje ke bād āvāz thoṛī kam rakheṃge?
sentences.en: Would you keep the noise down a bit after ten at night?

sentences.native: मैं नीचे वाले फ़्लैट से हूँ, आपसे एक बात करनी थी।
sentences.roman: maiṃ nīche vāle flaiṭ se hūṃ, āpse ek bāt karnī thī.
sentences.en: I'm from the flat downstairs, I wanted to have a word with you.

sentences.native: आप हमारे नए पड़ोसी हैं? कोई ज़रूरत हो तो बताइएगा।
sentences.roman: āp hamāre naye paṛosī haiṃ? koī zarūrat ho to batāiyegā.
sentences.en: You're our new neighbours? If you need anything, do let us know.

sentences.native: इस मोहल्ले में सब लोग बहुत अच्छे हैं।
sentences.roman: is mohalle meṃ sab log bahut achchhe haiṃ.
sentences.en: Everyone in this neighbourhood is really nice.

sentences.native: शिकायत करने से पहले एक बार उनसे बात कर लो।
sentences.roman: shikāyat karne se pahle ek bār unse bāt kar lo.
sentences.en: Have a word with them once before you complain. (to a friend)

lessons.title: Moving house

tip.title: शिफ़्ट करना — English word + करना
tip.body:
- Moving house is **शिफ़्ट करना** (or **शिफ़्ट होना** 'to get moved in'). Hindi takes the English word and adds **करना**: **पैकिंग करना**, **टेंपो करना** 'to hire a tempo'.
- The **करना** part does all the grammar: शिफ़्ट **कर रहे हैं**, शिफ़्ट **हुए** हैं.

new: हम अगले महीने शिफ़्ट कर रहे हैं।
हम ऊपर वाले फ़्लैट में रहते हैं।

sentences.native: हम रविवार को नए फ़्लैट में शिफ़्ट कर रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: ham ravivār ko naye flaiṭ meṃ shifṭ kar rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: We're moving to the new flat on Sunday.

sentences.native: हम पिछले हफ़्ते ही शिफ़्ट हुए हैं।
sentences.roman: ham pichhle hafte hī shifṭ hue haiṃ.
sentences.en: We only moved in last week.

sentences.native: सामान के लिए एक टेंपो करना पड़ेगा।
sentences.roman: sāmān ke liye ek ṭempo karnā paṛegā.
sentences.en: We'll have to hire a tempo for the stuff.

sentences.native: टेंपो वाला कितने पैसे ले रहा है?
sentences.roman: ṭempo vālā kitne paise le rahā hai?
sentences.en: How much is the tempo guy charging?

sentences.native: पैकिंग में मेरी मदद करोगे?
sentences.roman: paiking meṃ merī madad karoge?
sentences.en: Will you help me with the packing? (to a friend)

sentences.native: पैकिंग अभी तक ख़त्म नहीं हुई!
sentences.roman: paiking abhī tak xatm nahīṃ huī!
sentences.en: The packing still isn't done!

sentences.native: जाने से पहले मकान-मालिक से एडवांस वापस ले लेना।
sentences.roman: jāne se pahle makān-mālik se eḍvāns vāpas le lenā.
sentences.en: Get your deposit back from the landlord before you leave.

sentences.native: मैंने बिजली का बिल भर दिया है।
sentences.roman: maiṃne bijlī kā bil bhar diyā hai.
sentences.en: I've paid the electricity bill.

sentences.native: नए फ़्लैट में गीज़र और पंखे लगवाने हैं।
sentences.roman: naye flaiṭ meṃ gīzar aur paṅkhe lagvāne haiṃ.
sentences.en: We need to get a geyser and fans put in the new flat.
